first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding currently has the strongest fit because it directly targets the 4% completion decline and may also reverse the 6% activation decline. I would verify memory_86 for evidence beyond early adoption and memory_73 to compare pricing's acquisition lift against customer quality, retention, and margin risks. The final choice remains contingent on those source records.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. Verified evidence shows this directly improves the declining completion metric (+13%), accelerates time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improves 30-day retention by 3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. It may also help reverse the activation decline. Promotional pricing is rejected despite short-term qualified-revenue lift because verified retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal. Uncertainty remains about whether prior onboarding gains will replicate at current baselines, so an experiment is preferable to broad rollout.
